fixed: peak throughput across the batch sweep, at each thread count
note: One process per thread count. torch.set_num_threads does not reliably resize a thread pool that has already run work, so measuring several counts inside one process silently reports the first one several times.

reproducibility.note: Two clean runs of the same sweep. The 1-thread baseline moved 16% between them (2.29 then 2.66), which carries into every speedup because it is the denominator. It is the noisiest point by construction: longest per-sample time, so fewest samples inside the per-point budget. The rows at 4, 8 and 10 threads agree within 5%. So the SHAPE reproduces and the third significant figure does not, and the honest claim is a range.

discarded_run.why: Taken immediately after an interrupted sweep, almost certainly against an orphaned child process competing for cores. Recorded here rather than deleted: it is the reason the sweep was repeated at all, and a measurement you threw away is part of the method.
